systematicReviews.title: Mindfulness-based programmes for mental health promotion in adults in nonclinical settings: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
systematicReviews.population: 11605 adults in 136 randomized trials across 29 countries; 77 percent women
systematicReviews.method: Preregistered systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of expert-defined in-person programs
systematicReviews.finding: Programs outperformed no intervention for several average outcomes, but did not show superiority to specific active controls and effects varied across settings.
systematicReviews.limitations: GRADE confidence ranged from moderate to very low, many trials had high risk of bias, prediction intervals included no effect, and the studied multi-session teacher-led programs are not equivalent to a brief Motazen exercise.

systematicReviews.title: Individual Resilience Interventions: A Systematic Review in Adult Population Samples over the Last Decade
systematicReviews.organization: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
systematicReviews.population: Adult samples across 38 controlled intervention articles
systematicReviews.method: PRISMA-guided systematic review of randomized and nonrandomized controlled studies
systematicReviews.finding: Many studies reported statistically significant results, but definitions, methods, populations, and interventions varied greatly.
systematicReviews.limitations: Samples often lacked power, methodological quality was fair, and heterogeneity prevented meaningful meta-analysis. Resilience must not be framed as a stable trait or an individual duty to tolerate harmful conditions.

systematicReviews.title: The impact of psychological treatment on intolerance of uncertainty in generalized anxiety disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: 1199 adults with generalized anxiety disorder across 26 eligible studies
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review and meta-analysis of evidence-based psychological treatments
systematicReviews.finding: Psychological treatments reduced intolerance of uncertainty and related symptoms in adults with generalized anxiety disorder.
systematicReviews.limitations: This is clinical treatment evidence for diagnosed GAD, not proof that a general literacy lesson treats anxiety. Apparent superiority of directly targeted CBT was not maintained at follow-up.

systematicReviews.title: Effectiveness of psychological treatments for depressive disorders in primary care: systematic review and meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: 5159 adults with depression in 30 primary-care trials
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis by therapy and delivery mode
systematicReviews.finding: Psychological treatments overall showed benefit, while the estimate for face-to-face problem-solving therapy crossed no effect in this synthesis.
systematicReviews.limitations: Clinical treatment evidence does not validate a general problem-solving worksheet as treatment. Therapy type, delivery, comparator, and population affect estimates.

systematicReviews.title: Debiasing Health-Related Judgments and Decision Making: A Systematic Review
systematicReviews.population: Lay people and health professionals in 87 studies reported across 68 articles
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review of experimental and quasi-experimental debiasing interventions
systematicReviews.finding: Most interventions were at least partially successful, but strategies, target biases, outcomes, and study quality varied.
systematicReviews.limitations: Students dominated samples, many reports omitted power or measurement-quality information, and partial short-term task success does not establish durable transfer to consequential everyday decisions.

systematicReviews.title: Understanding experiences of mental health help-seeking in Arab populations around the world: a systematic review and narrative synthesis
systematicReviews.population: Arab adults represented in 74 included articles across Arab countries and diaspora settings
systematicReviews.method: Prospectively registered systematic review with narrative synthesis
systematicReviews.finding: Reported barriers included stigma, privacy and confidentiality, trust, literacy, language, logistics, and culture, while informal family and friend support was often preferred.
systematicReviews.limitations: Most studies measured attitudes or intentions rather than actual use, Arab populations and settings are heterogeneous, and regional synthesis cannot be used as an Egyptian prevalence estimate.

systematicReviews.title: Investigating the effects of marriage and relationship education on couples' communication skills: a meta-analytic study
systematicReviews.population: Couples represented in 143 evaluations from 97 relationship-education reports
systematicReviews.method: Meta-analysis of marriage and relationship education evaluations
systematicReviews.finding: The synthesis found modest communication effects that differed by participant distress, follow-up, and measurement method.
systematicReviews.limitations: Older couple-program evidence does not establish that a short generic script improves every relationship or transfers across culture, power imbalance, coercion, or violence.

systematicReviews.title: The effectiveness of assertiveness communication training programs for healthcare professionals and students: A systematic review
systematicReviews.population: Healthcare professionals and students in eight included papers
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review with independent quality appraisal
systematicReviews.finding: Training showed some benefits, while behavioral outcomes were mainly assessed in simulation and evidence for sustained behavior and safety outcomes remained limited.
systematicReviews.limitations: Small occupational evidence base cannot validate a universal boundary script or assume that speaking up is equally safe across hierarchies, families, workplaces, and abusive contexts.

systematicReviews.title: Do relationship education programs reduce relationship aggression? A meta-analytic study
systematicReviews.population: 25527 participants across 31 relationship-education studies
systematicReviews.method: Meta-analysis of control trials and pre-post studies
systematicReviews.finding: The overall association with reduced aggression was small, and the randomized-trial estimate was not statistically significant while pre-post estimates were larger.
systematicReviews.limitations: Combining designs complicates causal interpretation. Relationship education must not be presented as a safety response to active coercion or violence, which requires survivor-centered assessment and services.

systematicReviews.title: Forgiveness Therapy for the Promotion of Mental Well-Being: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
systematicReviews.population: Adolescents and adults in randomized trials after varied interpersonal hurts or violence
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review and meta-analysis of process-based forgiveness interventions
systematicReviews.finding: Structured process-based interventions showed average improvements in several wellbeing outcomes and forgiveness measures.
systematicReviews.limitations: Therapy evidence does not create a duty to forgive, reconcile, contact, remain with, or confront a person who caused harm. Safety and autonomy take priority.

systematicReviews.title: Impacts of digital social media detox for mental health: A systematic review and meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: Participants in ten digital-detox studies published from 2013 through 2023
systematicReviews.method: PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis with risk-of-bias appraisal
systematicReviews.finding: The synthesis found a small reduction in depressive symptoms but no statistically significant average effects for life satisfaction, stress, or overall wellbeing.
systematicReviews.limitations: Only ten heterogeneous studies were included, detox definitions varied, and mental-health outcomes cannot be attributed to screen minutes alone.

systematicReviews.title: Psychological Inoculation for Credibility Assessment, Sharing Intention, and Discernment of Misinformation: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
systematicReviews.population: 42530 participants across 42 independent studies
systematicReviews.method: PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis with moderator analyses
systematicReviews.finding: Inoculation produced small improvements in credibility and sharing discernment, but did not significantly reduce misinformation sharing intention overall.
systematicReviews.limitations: Task performance and intention are not durable real-world sharing behavior; English-language studies and intervention-specific findings require cultural and Arabic-language testing.

systematicReviews.title: Interventions designed to improve financial capability: A systematic review
systematicReviews.population: Participants in 24 unique financial-capability studies conducted in OECD countries
systematicReviews.method: Comprehensive systematic review of randomized and quasi-experimental interventions combining education with a product or service
systematicReviews.finding: The review found insufficient comparable evidence to conclude that financial-capability interventions reliably improve financial behavior or outcomes.
systematicReviews.limitations: Evidence was sparse, heterogeneous, and limited to OECD settings; personal education cannot overcome low income, inflation, debt terms, labor conditions, or missing consumer protections.

systematicReviews.title: Organizational interventions and occupational burnout: a meta-analysis with focus on exhaustion
systematicReviews.organization: International Archives of Occupational and Environmental Health
systematicReviews.population: Active workers in 13 organizational or combined intervention studies
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis with GRADE appraisal
systematicReviews.finding: Organizational and combined interventions produced a small average reduction in exhaustion.
systematicReviews.limitations: Evidence quality was very low with heterogeneity, bias risk, and few studies. Individual coping advice must not displace workload, schedule, control, safety, or organizational responsibility.

systematicReviews.title: A Meta-Analytic Review of Interventions That Promote Meaning in Life
systematicReviews.population: Participants in 33 randomized controlled trials of meaning-in-life interventions
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis by intervention and control type
systematicReviews.finding: Meaning-in-life outcomes improved on average, with much larger estimates against passive than active controls and considerable heterogeneity.
systematicReviews.limitations: Meaning is culturally and personally plural; heterogeneous effects do not justify prescribing one purpose, moral hierarchy, career path, or spiritual frame.

systematicReviews.title: Exploring the Effects of Volunteering on the Social, Mental, and Physical Health and Well-being of Volunteers: An Umbrella Review
systematicReviews.population: Participants represented in 28 reviews, mainly older adults in the United States
systematicReviews.method: Prospectively registered umbrella review with AMSTAR 2 quality appraisal
systematicReviews.finding: Reviews reported benefits across several domains, but review quality was generally poor and populations were concentrated among older US adults.
systematicReviews.limitations: Selection, access, health status, role quality, unpaid-labor burden, and preexisting motivation complicate causal interpretation; volunteering must remain optional and non-exploitative.

systematicReviews.title: The State of Web Accessibility for People with Cognitive Disabilities: A Rapid Evidence Assessment
systematicReviews.population: People age nine and older living with cognitive impairment represented in 45 papers
systematicReviews.method: Systematic rapid evidence assessment across three databases
systematicReviews.finding: Persistent barriers remain despite standards, and meaningful solutions require attention to lived experience, tools, and inclusive research practice.
systematicReviews.limitations: The evidence base is heterogeneous and cannot replace direct participation by Arabic-speaking Egyptian users with varied disabilities.

systematicReviews.title: Retrieval Practice Consistently Benefits Student Learning: A Systematic Review of Applied Research in Schools and Classrooms
systematicReviews.population: 5374 learners across 50 experiments in applied school and classroom settings
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review with 49 coded effect sizes from classroom research
systematicReviews.finding: Retrieval practice improved later learning across varied classroom conditions, with 57 percent of effects reported as medium or large.
systematicReviews.limitations: Only 6 percent of experiments were conducted in non-WEIRD countries; school and classroom test performance does not establish adult Egyptian behavior change or clinical benefit.

systematicReviews.title: Transfer of test-enhanced learning: Meta-analytic review and synthesis
systematicReviews.population: 10382 participants represented in 122 experiments and 192 transfer effect sizes
systematicReviews.method: Meta-analytic review of published and unpublished experiments across more than 40 years
systematicReviews.finding: Practice testing produced a moderate average transfer benefit relative to re-exposure, but transfer varied strongly with task congruence, elaboration, and initial retrieval success.
systematicReviews.limitations: Bias-adjusted intercepts were substantially smaller and sometimes indicated no positive transfer when favorable moderators were absent; knowledge transfer is not real-world behavior change.

systematicReviews.title: The Distributed Practice Effect on Classroom Learning: A Meta-Analytic Review of Applied Research
systematicReviews.population: More than 3000 learners represented in 22 reports and 31 classroom effect sizes
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review and meta-analysis of curriculum-relevant classroom studies
systematicReviews.finding: Distributed practice showed a moderate average advantage over massed practice for classroom learning.
systematicReviews.limitations: The small study pool prevented a comprehensive moderator analysis; classroom retention evidence does not determine one ideal spacing schedule for Motazen or prove behavioral transfer.

systematicReviews.title: The efficacy of microlearning in improving self-care capability: a systematic review of the literature
systematicReviews.population: People of varied ages represented in 26 controlled microlearning studies
systematicReviews.method: PRISMA-reported systematic review with Cochrane and ROBINS-I risk-of-bias appraisal
systematicReviews.finding: Microlearning often improved cognitive self-care outcomes, while actual self-care behavior improved in only a minority of studies that measured it.
systematicReviews.limitations: Twenty-five of 26 studies had moderate-to-high risk of bias; the evidence does not establish a universal lesson length, daily dose, or reliable behavior change.

systematicReviews.title: Attrition and adherence in smartphone-delivered interventions for mental health problems: A systematic and meta-analytic review
systematicReviews.organization: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
systematicReviews.population: Participants in 70 randomized controlled trials of smartphone-delivered mental-health interventions
systematicReviews.method: Systematic and meta-analytic review of trial attrition and qualitative synthesis of adherence
systematicReviews.finding: Average study attrition was substantial and intervention use commonly declined over time; no participant baseline characteristic reliably predicted attrition.
systematicReviews.limitations: Clinical intervention trials are not equivalent to an educational curriculum, and reminders or compensation associated with retention do not justify manipulative engagement design.

systematicReviews.title: Retention and Engagement in Culturally Adapted Digital Mental Health Interventions: Systematic Review of Dropout, Attrition, and Adherence in Non-WEIRD Settings
systematicReviews.population: 4656 adults across 23 randomized trials of culturally adapted digital mental-health interventions in non-WEIRD settings
systematicReviews.method: PRISMA-guided systematic review of attrition, dropout, adherence, adaptation depth, and methodological quality
systematicReviews.finding: Deeper participatory adaptation was associated with more favorable retention than surface translation alone in the included trials.
systematicReviews.limitations: The evidence is associative across heterogeneous clinical interventions, not proof that adaptation causes retention or that the reported figures transfer to Egypt or Motazen.

systematicReviews.title: Teach-back: A systematic review of implementation and impacts
systematicReviews.population: Patients and clinicians represented in health-service teach-back studies
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review of implementation strategies, fidelity, and knowledge or self-care impacts
systematicReviews.finding: Teach-back can support knowledge and self-care in clinical communication, while implementation and fidelity reporting are inconsistent.
systematicReviews.limitations: Motazen cannot conduct clinician-patient teach-back; it can only adapt the nonjudgmental comprehension-check principle and must test it directly in Arabic.

systematicReviews.title: Emotion differentiation and behavioral dysregulation in clinical and nonclinical samples: A meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: Clinical and nonclinical participants across 17 studies
systematicReviews.method: Meta-analysis of negative emotion differentiation and maladaptive behaviors
systematicReviews.finding: Greater negative-emotion differentiation was associated with slightly less maladaptive behavior on average, including after controlling for negative affect.
systematicReviews.limitations: The association was small, studies were methodologically heterogeneous, and association does not prove that teaching labels changes behavior.

systematicReviews.title: Shedding light on the association between repetitive negative thinking and deficits in cognitive control: A meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: Clinical and nonclinical participants represented in 94 studies
systematicReviews.method: Meta-analysis of repetitive negative thinking and multiple cognitive-control functions
systematicReviews.finding: Repetitive negative thinking had a small association with difficulty discarding no-longer-relevant material from working memory, but not with the other tested control functions.
systematicReviews.limitations: Primary studies and cognitive paradigms had reliability and sample-size limitations; the result rejects a broad claim that rumination reflects a global control deficit.

systematicReviews.title: Health effects of psychological interventions for worry and rumination: A meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: Participants in 36 randomized studies of nonpharmacological interventions targeting perseverative cognition
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of rumination, worry, physical, and behavioral outcomes
systematicReviews.finding: Interventions reduced rumination and worry on average, while corresponding behavior and physical-health effects were smaller and professional delivery was associated with larger cognitive effects.
systematicReviews.limitations: No intervention type clearly outperformed alternatives; treatment evidence must not be reframed as proof that a self-guided literacy lesson treats persistent rumination.

systematicReviews.title: Effects of stress on decisions under uncertainty: A meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: 1829 adult participants across 32 laboratory stress datasets
systematicReviews.method: Random-effects meta-analysis of experimentally induced stress and decisions under uncertainty
systematicReviews.finding: Laboratory stress produced a small average shift toward more disadvantageous, reward-seeking, or risky choices, with effects dependent on situation and stressor type.
systematicReviews.limitations: The effect was small and laboratory tasks have limited ecological validity; stress does not make every person or decision uniformly irrational.

systematicReviews.title: The effects of sleep deprivation on risky decision making
systematicReviews.population: Healthy adults in experimental sleep-deprivation and risky-choice studies
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review of risky decision-making effects and moderators
systematicReviews.finding: Sleep deprivation had complex, inconsistent effects on risky decisions that varied with framing, task, duration, timing, sex, and other conditions.
systematicReviews.limitations: The evidence does not support a deterministic claim that one poor night always causes riskier choices, and laboratory tasks may not represent daily decisions.

systematicReviews.title: 20th Anniversary Update of the Ottawa Decision Support Framework Part 1: A Systematic Review of the Decisional Needs of People Making Health or Social Decisions
systematicReviews.population: Decision makers, families, and practitioners across 45 health and social decision studies in seven countries
systematicReviews.method: Mixed-studies systematic review with independent screening, quality appraisal, and narrative synthesis
systematicReviews.finding: Decision needs include knowledge, values, support, roles, timing, expectations, information overload, powerful emotions, and family or practitioner involvement.
systematicReviews.limitations: The framework centers health and social decisions and cannot be copied into every everyday choice; only peer-reviewed ODSF-based studies were included.

systematicReviews.title: Can There Ever Be Too Many Options? A Meta-Analytic Review of Choice Overload
systematicReviews.population: 5036 participants across 63 conditions from 50 published and unpublished choice experiments
systematicReviews.method: Meta-analytic review of motivation, choice, and satisfaction under larger versus smaller option sets
systematicReviews.finding: The mean choice-overload effect was approximately zero with substantial between-study variation and no sufficient universal condition identified.
systematicReviews.limitations: Consumer-choice experiments do not cover all high-stakes or personal decisions; contextual moderators may still produce overload in some settings.

systematicReviews.title: The effect of caffeine on subsequent sleep: A systematic review and meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: Participants across 24 experimental caffeine and nighttime-sleep studies
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review and meta-analysis of caffeine dose, timing, and objective or subjective sleep outcomes
systematicReviews.finding: Caffeine reduced total sleep and sleep efficiency on average, with dose- and timing-relevant effects.
systematicReviews.limitations: Average timing estimates depend on dose, beverage, metabolism, medication, pregnancy, age, tolerance, and bedtime; they are not a universal curfew or medical instruction.

systematicReviews.title: The association of screen time and the risk of sleep outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: 548338 participants across 21 cohort studies and diverse age groups
systematicReviews.method: Preregistered systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of screen time and sleep outcomes
systematicReviews.finding: Longer screen time was associated with shorter sleep, later bedtime, and more sleep difficulties on average.
systematicReviews.limitations: Cohort associations do not prove that screen exposure alone caused sleep outcomes; activity type, timing, displacement, content, work, and reverse causation matter.

systematicReviews.title: A meta-analysis of techniques to promote motivation for health behaviour change from a self-determination theory perspective
systematicReviews.population: Children and adults across 74 controlled health-behavior intervention studies; 80 percent were randomized or cluster-randomized
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of need-supportive techniques and self-determination mediators
systematicReviews.finding: Need-supportive interventions improved perceived autonomy support, autonomy, competence, relatedness, and motivation on average, while individual techniques had limited independent impact and appeared to work in combinations.
systematicReviews.limitations: The review concerns intervention mediators rather than a universal recipe for action, combines ages and behaviors, and does not validate a self-guided Egyptian curriculum.

systematicReviews.title: Self-determination theory interventions for health behavior change: Meta-analysis and meta-analytic structural equation modeling of randomized controlled trials
systematicReviews.organization: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
systematicReviews.population: Participants in randomized controlled health-behavior interventions based on self-determination theory
systematicReviews.method: Meta-analysis and meta-analytic structural equation modeling of randomized controlled trials
systematicReviews.finding: Self-determination interventions produced a small average improvement in health behavior, with autonomous motivation and perceived competence among the tested mediating pathways.
systematicReviews.limitations: The average behavioral effect was small; health-behavior trials do not show that motivation must precede every action or that one technique works for everyone.

systematicReviews.title: Does the Mere Presence of a Smartphone Impact Cognitive Performance? A Meta-Analysis of the Brain Drain Effect
systematicReviews.population: 7093 participants across 56 effects from smartphone-presence studies
systematicReviews.method: Preregistered systematic review and six meta-analyses by cognitive outcome
systematicReviews.finding: Only working-memory capacity showed a significant pooled negative effect; other cognitive outcomes were null, and methodological heterogeneity and low power limited inference.
systematicReviews.limitations: Laboratory mere-presence manipulations do not cover active notifications, compulsive checking, content, or every real-world work context.

systematicReviews.title: Digital self-control interventions for distracting media multitasking: A systematic review
systematicReviews.population: Users and learners in studies of software-based digital self-control interventions
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review of intervention mechanisms, behavior, cognitive control, and performance outcomes
systematicReviews.finding: Intervention mechanisms and effects varied; usage visualization alone was often ineffective, blocking strictness mattered, and the evidence did not establish digital self-control tools as a categorical solution.
systematicReviews.limitations: Evidence was sparse, frequently student-centered, and heterogeneous; tools may create burden, work conflicts, avoidance, or compensatory use.

systematicReviews.title: Social media use and well-being: What we know and what we need to know
systematicReviews.population: Social-media users across hundreds of studies included in 27 reviews published from 2019 through August 2021
systematicReviews.method: Umbrella review of nine meta-analyses, nine systematic reviews, and nine narrative reviews
systematicReviews.finding: Reviews drawing from overlapping evidence reached disagreeing conclusions, especially for time spent and active versus passive use, emphasizing person-specific and methodological variation.
systematicReviews.limitations: An umbrella synthesis inherits weaknesses of its reviews and cannot identify an individual user's cause or optimal usage rule.

systematicReviews.title: Anger and emotion regulation strategies: a meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: Clinical and nonclinical participants across 81 studies and 115 effect sizes
systematicReviews.method: Meta-analysis of associations between anger and avoidance, acceptance, distraction, reappraisal, rumination, and suppression
systematicReviews.finding: Anger was positively associated with avoidance, rumination, and suppression and negatively associated with acceptance and reappraisal, but heterogeneity was large across every analysis.
systematicReviews.limitations: Associations do not establish that teaching one strategy will prevent aggression; effects varied by anger type, clinical and criminal status, culture, study quality, and sample composition.

systematicReviews.title: A meta-analytic review of anger management activities that increase or decrease arousal: What fuels or douses rage?
systematicReviews.population: 10189 participants across 154 studies and 184 independent samples
systematicReviews.method: Meta-analytic review comparing arousal-decreasing and arousal-increasing anger-management activities
systematicReviews.finding: Arousal-decreasing activities reduced anger and aggression on average, whereas arousal-increasing activities were ineffective overall and did not support venting as an anger-reduction strategy.
systematicReviews.limitations: The synthesis combines distinct activities, populations, delivery modes, and outcomes; it does not make every breathing or meditation exercise universally safe or replace violence-risk assessment.

systematicReviews.title: Adverse events in meditation practices and meditation-based therapies: a systematic review
systematicReviews.population: Adults across experimental, observational, and case reports of meditation practices or therapies
systematicReviews.method: Broad-sweep systematic review of somatic, psychiatric, neurological, and cognitive adverse events
systematicReviews.finding: Adverse experiences were reported across study types, including anxiety, depression, cognitive anomalies, fear, dissociation, trauma re-experience, and rare severe events; estimates varied greatly by study design.
systematicReviews.limitations: Retrospective reports, case studies, retreat exposure, inconsistent definitions, selection, attribution, and sparse longitudinal data prevent a precise Motazen risk estimate.

systematicReviews.title: The empirical status of mindfulness-based interventions: A systematic review of 44 meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials
systematicReviews.population: Participants across 44 meta-analyses of randomized mindfulness-based intervention trials
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review of randomized-trial meta-analyses covering effects, heterogeneity, bias, moderators, and harms reporting
systematicReviews.finding: Benefits varied by population, comparator, and outcome, while adverse-event reporting was inconsistent and often absent from the underlying evidence.
systematicReviews.limitations: A review of reviews inherits overlap, reporting gaps, and heterogeneity and does not establish the safety or efficacy of an unguided micro-practice for a particular user.

systematicReviews.title: Identity Development and Well-being: A Systematic Review
systematicReviews.organization: Studia Doctoralia Psychology and Educational Science
systematicReviews.population: Participants in 10 identity-development and wellbeing studies published from 1990 through 2024
systematicReviews.method: PRISMA systematic review across five databases and reference lists
systematicReviews.finding: Identity commitment related to identity development, but findings for in-depth exploration were inconsistent and the identity-wellbeing relationship remained unclear.
systematicReviews.limitations: Only 10 studies met criteria, cultural and age transfer are uncertain, and the evidence does not validate an identity-building exercise or a fixed ideal self.

systematicReviews.title: Adult friendship and wellbeing: A systematic review with practical implications
systematicReviews.population: Adults aged 18 to 65 across 38 studies, predominantly young adults and university students
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review of adult friendship variables and multidimensional wellbeing
systematicReviews.finding: Friendship quality, socializing, supportive reactions, autonomy support, and maintenance efforts were commonly associated with wellbeing, while evidence was often sparse, contradictory, or population-specific.
systematicReviews.limitations: Most evidence was cross-sectional and student-heavy, friend dyads and longitudinal studies were rare, and association does not justify pressure to make or keep unsafe friendships.

systematicReviews.title: Does time management work? A meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: 53957 participants across 158 nonclinical quantitative studies
systematicReviews.method: Broad meta-analysis of time-management measures, experiments, performance, wellbeing, and contextual correlates
systematicReviews.finding: Time management had moderate associations with wellbeing and performance and a somewhat stronger relationship with wellbeing, but most studies were cross-sectional and interventions were poorly specified.
systematicReviews.limitations: Causality is limited, heterogeneity is high, and access to controllable time depends on income, education, care work, job autonomy, and privilege.

systematicReviews.title: Examining the relationship between civic engagement and mental health in young adults: a systematic review of the literature
systematicReviews.population: Young adults across 53 civic-engagement and wellbeing studies
systematicReviews.method: Systematic review and narrative synthesis across civic activity types, duration, directionality, mediators, and moderators
systematicReviews.finding: Civic engagement had heterogeneous positive, negative, and null relationships with wellbeing depending on activity, duration, directionality, adversity, and participant context.
systematicReviews.limitations: Young-adult evidence does not establish causal benefit, safety, political neutrality, or feasibility in Egypt and cannot justify compulsory participation.

systematicReviews.title: Are Ethics Training Programs Improving? A Meta-Analytic Review of Past and Present Ethics Instruction in the Sciences
systematicReviews.population: 10069 participants across 66 empirical studies, 106 science-ethics courses, and 150 effect sizes
systematicReviews.method: Random-effects meta-analytic review including published and unpublished ethics-training evaluations
systematicReviews.finding: Ethics instruction showed moderate average benefits, with stronger effects for knowledge, self-perception, and ethical decision making and important variation by field, criterion, practice, and course design.
systematicReviews.limitations: Science and professional ethics courses cannot define a universal personal morality, prove real-world ethical behavior, or transfer directly to Egyptian civic and family dilemmas.

systematicReviews.title: Self-esteem Interventions in Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: Adults across 119 intervention studies
systematicReviews.method: Random-effects systematic review and meta-analysis of interventions targeting adult global self-esteem
systematicReviews.finding: Interventions had a small-to-moderate average effect on measured global self-esteem, with substantial variation by intervention, format, contact, population, and comparator.
systematicReviews.limitations: Heterogeneity, confounding between moderators, limited power, publication bias, and emphasis on the target measure prevent equating higher self-esteem scores with self-respect or broad wellbeing.

systematicReviews.title: Effectiveness of Error Management Training: A Meta-analysis
systematicReviews.population: 2183 participants across 24 identified training studies
systematicReviews.method: Meta-analysis comparing error-management, error-avoidant, and exploratory training conditions
systematicReviews.finding: Error-management training showed a positive average training effect with larger estimates for transfer and novel tasks; active exploration and explicit error encouragement were candidate effective elements.
systematicReviews.limitations: Controlled skill-training errors are not equivalent to bereavement, trauma, injustice, moral injury, irreversible loss, or high-stakes real-world failure.

systematicReviews.title: Do Growth Mindset Interventions Impact Students' Academic Achievement? A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis With Recommendations for Best Practices
systematicReviews.population: 97672 students across 63 studies; smaller subsets met manipulation and higher-quality criteria
systematicReviews.method: Best-practice appraisal and three meta-analyses with publication-bias and study-quality checks
systematicReviews.finding: The overall achievement effect was very small and became nonsignificant after publication-bias correction; higher-quality and successful-manipulation subsets were nonsignificant.
systematicReviews.limitations: The review concerns student achievement, not all forms of learning, recovery, accountability, or adult adaptation after setbacks.

systematicReviews.title: Psychosocial Family Interventions for Relatives of People Living With Psychotic Disorders in the Arab World: Systematic Review
systematicReviews.population: Six family-intervention studies from Arab-region clinical settings
systematicReviews.method: Five-database systematic review and narrative synthesis of culturally adapted family interventions
systematicReviews.finding: The small evidence base suggested culturally adapted family intervention was feasible and acceptable, but included-study quality was generally poor and the domain was narrowly clinical.
systematicReviews.limitations: Only six studies, clinical psychosis focus, generally poor methodological quality, and regional aggregation prevent transfer to everyday Egyptian family guidance.
